findings.summary: OutSpec's docstring says E = tol comes from the exact partial sums and each chunk's largest lifted product; it now also uses each chunk's exact magnitude (chunkAbs, the second arm)
findings.detail: OutSpec, in the spec item, describes its tolerance as 'the error bound over the loop's 2*cdiv(K, 64) chunks of 32 products, from the exact partial sums and each chunk's largest lifted product'. That was all of errAt's inputs before this change. errAt now takes min(rho*(X_j + E_j), kappa*A_j + rho'*(X_j + E_j)) with A_j = chunkAbs p j, the chunk's exact sum of |a*b|, and the second arm is what makes the tolerance small after a large early product (1.55% instead of 13.7% of |X| at K = 512). A reader of Post alone would think the bound ignores the chunks' magnitudes. tol's own docstring and errAt's are right. Adding 'and each chunk's exact magnitude' to OutSpec's docstring would resolve it.
findings.evidence: Defs.lean, OutSpec's docstring against errAt and tol (claim.md, section 4).

notes: Re-review of spec and assumption:dot after the move to DotE5m2ChunkLoss, at gate 752f03b36e81309e. assumption:dot: DotE5m2ChunkLoss P = DotF8ChunkLoss P .f8e5 .f8e5, the num.md fp8 tl.dot listing's alternative, for any input precision with maxImpreciseAcc 2^30, which matches the model's line 300. Its docstring states the fact as the library does. spec: errAt is the minimum composed per chunk with the fact's constants (rho 2^-7, sigma 2^-12, alpha 2^-126, kappa 2, rho' 2^-12) and chunkAbs of the unlifted products. It is explicit and computable. The work file ChunkLoss proves errAt = Dot8Chunk.errM on the loop's chunks (from 0, the chunk sums, chunkAbs, chunkMax), so the tolerance is the library's composed bound. It also proves errAt <= the round-24 recursion at every chunk, so Post only got stronger, and zero_rejected and drop_rejected still hold. main, consistent, satisfiable, tol_spike, zero_rejected, drop_rejected and tol_le_tolA depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. I checked the figures by exact rational evaluation (work file chunkloss_figs.py), and all hold. One product 1 at K-1: 0.8057% at 512 and 4096. tol_spike: the maximum over all covered K is 0.8549% = 71713/2^23, attained. drop_rejected s = 0: 0.0268 -> 0.0165 (K = 512) and 0.0658 -> 0.0175 (K = 4096). One product at 0: 13.70% -> 1.547% and 179.3% -> 7.253%. All ones: 6.303% and 73.91%, unchanged, with no chunk on the second arm; X_j + E_j reaches at most 7035 against the threshold 8192/31 * 32 = 8456. First chunk 1s, then 1/16s: matches with both row and column 1/16, products 2^-8: 12.46% -> 11.83% and 142.7% -> 73.73%. The x = y = 1.25 float16 bound: 0.01413 < 0.015 worst covered, 0.01336 < 0.014 at 512. The 'about 2^8 A_j' threshold is 8192/31 = 264, proved in the work file. randn (the script's seed 0, fp16 randn cast to float8e5 on GPU 0, 512 rows at K = 512 and 120 at 4096): no chunk takes the second arm and new/old = 1 exactly, so 'unchanged' holds. My 20-draw medians spread over tol 0.88-1.76 and |S| 9.6-21.1 at 512, and tol 41-57 and |S| 27-51 at 4096; the README's 1.5 (20.5) and 52 (52) lie within that spread.
